trace.topic: We Have 30 AI Agents in Production. Here Are the Top 5 Issues No One Talks About
trace.goal: Surface hidden operational problems with multi-agent deployment.
expected_facts: The answer should focus on real operational friction, not futuristic speculation.
It should cover issues like supervision, drift, orchestration, or workflow brittleness.
It should frame these as solvable but under-discussed execution challenges.
rubric_must_haves: Keeps the focus on operating reality.
Includes at least one issue beyond prompt quality alone.
trace.gold_reference: A strong answer should explain that once many AI agents are live, the hard problems shift from demos to operations: monitoring, coordination, reliability, stale data, and human oversight. The point is that multi-agent systems create a new management surface area that most teams underestimate. Founders should treat these as production issues, not side notes.
trace.prompt:
Write a blog post in the style of Jason Lemkin about: We Have 30 AI Agents in Production. Here Are the Top 5 Issues No One Talks About

Style examples from train-owned source text.
Use them for voice only. They are not evidence for claims.
Do not copy long passages verbatim.
[Style 1]
Dear SaaStr: How Can You Ensure a Smooth Transition When A New Team Member Takes Over a Customer Account?
Add value in the first interaction.  This is so rare.
There’s nothing more frustrating than getting a random email, “Hi, Tony is gone from the company. I know nothing about you, but I’m your new rep. Can we schedule a call?”
Find some way to add value.
One great way is to demo upcoming features / an upcoming release.
“Hi, I’m Jason, your next account exec. I’d love to find a way to help even more. Can I show you or anyone on your team the new AI features we’re launching shortly? There’s no additional cost for them and based on what I can see, they may radically increase your efficiency.”
Not perfect. But much better.
A second, albeit riskier, way to add value is to set up a call asking for “honest feedback on how we’re doing.”
This works, too.  Customers often just want to be heard.  The “problem” is you might have to do something about it.
[Style 2]
Dear SaaStr: When Is It Too Soon to Target Enterprise Customers in SaaS?
It too soon to target enterprise clients when you can’t support their needs 90 days
after
you close them.
It’s sort of OK in the enterprise to promise features and functionality that are sort of there … so long as you deliver them fairly promptly after the deal closes.
In fact, it happens all the time. Enterprise customers will even sign contracts agreeing to buy so long as you implement a key feature with X number of days.
But if you don’t have the team, commitment and experience to deliver that functionality at least X days after you close a Big Customer … you aren’t ready.  They’ll churn or at least, never fully deploy.
You don’t have to have the full enterprise package in the early days to close enterprise customers, especially if they have interest in you.  You’ll get some slack as a new, emerging vendor.  Especially if you have a strong deployment team.
But you have to meet your commitments and promises to them fairly soon after the deal closes.

trace.answer:
We’ve been running 30+ AI agents across our entire GTM stack since late January — RevOps, outbound sales, inbound qualification, content generation, event management, ticketing, sponsorship, and more. Not pilots. Not experiments. Full production use cases that handle real customer interactions every single day. And here’s what nobody tells you before diving in:
the implementation challenges far outweigh any technical questions. Let me walk through each of these. Challenge #1: Context Switching Between Platforms
Here’s what most people miss entirely: switching between platforms creates cognitive load unlike anything else in traditional software. Think about it this way —
context switching costs money. Every time you move between tools, you lose productivity. When we were evaluating different vendors, one major provider had such severe context switching that it literally added hours to our evaluation process. Compare that to traditional software where everything lives within a single interface. Now imagine having eight separate interfaces spread across multiple tabs in Chrome. Then multiply that by three dozen agents. That’s what managing 30+ AI agents looks like today. Our solution? Create a dedicated browser tab group specifically for AI agent monitoring. Each platform gets its own tab, and we’ve trained ourselves to stay focused exclusively on those tabs during core work hours. If you catch yourself checking Slack messages while reviewing agent outputs, you’re wasting two things simultaneously: time and cognitive capacity. Challenge #2: Training Time Requirements vs. Reality
The hype around AI training sounds amazing until you actually sit down with a spreadsheet.

#5. Launch Your First AI Agent That Actually Works.  And That You Can Really Sell.
Not an AI feature. Not a chatbot. A real AI agent that handles actual workflows end-to-end.
I’ve deployed 20+ AI agents across SaaStr’s operations. Support agents. Content agents. Sales qualification agents. Together they’ve generated over $1M in revenue while reducing our headcount needs.
Most founders are still debating whether to add AI to their product. That’s table stakes now. The real question is: are you using AI agents to fundamentally transform your own operations?
Because here’s what I’m seeing: companies deploying working AI agents are operating with 30-50% fewer humans in key functions. Customer support. Sales development. Content creation. Implementation. Legal review.
Those aren’t future capabilities. They’re working today. At scale. And if you’re not deploying them, your competitors are.
Launch one high value agent in Q1. Get it working. Learn. Then launch two more by end of year.
The companies that figure out AI agents first will have massive cost advantages and speed advantages over everyone else. Don’t wait.
How we manage 20+ AI Agents without them stepping all over each other ...

Share all your challenges and metrics, and our AI will help come up with a game plan for you.

At SaaStr AI 2026, we answer that. With receipts.
